newsitem.title: UK: ACPC seeks proposals on coffee market stabilisation.
newsitem.headline: ACPC seeks proposals on coffee market stabilisation.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) has asked members to submit proposals on coffee market stabilisation plans to the secretariat by April 15, an ACPC official said.
The proposals will be examined by an ACPC technical group meeting at a date yet to be fixed, the official told Reuters.
It will be then submitted to the full ACPC council due to meet on May 21 in London, which also houses the secretariat.
The 14-member ACPC represents 80 percent of world production. The group's current one-year export programme aimed at limiting supplies through quota system expires at the end of June.
A Costa Rican delegate said at the ACPC technical meeting here on Thursday that some producers would seek a return to a trigger-price mechanism.
But exporters in Brazil, the leading ACPC member, said the move would send the wrong signal to consuming nations.
"This would just complicate things at a time when we should be trying to make things simpler," one said. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
